subject: general
question: In the architecture of a Central Processing Unit (CPU), which statement accurately distinguishes the function of the Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) from that of the Control Unit (CU)?

options.text: ALU decodes instructions, while CU handles data storage tasks.
CU executes arithmetic operations, and ALU controls program instructions.
CU interacts directly with peripheral devices, and ALU stores temporary data
ALU handles calculations and logic functions; CU manages instruction flow and coordination.

solution:
The correct answer is __**ALU handles calculations and logic functions; CU manages instruction flow and coordination.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU)** performs arithmetic operations (addition, subtraction, multiplication, etc.) and logical operations (AND, OR, NOT, etc.).
 
• The **Control Unit (CU)** directs the operation of the CPU by interpreting program instructions and coordinating the flow of data between the CPU, memory, and peripherals.
 
• While the ALU focuses on computation, the CU ensures the proper sequencing and execution of instructions.
 
• The CU does not perform calculations; its role is purely supervisory and organizational within the CPU architecture.
 
• The ALU and CU are integral components of the CPU, working together to ensure efficient data processing and program execution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Central Processing Unit (CPU):**

 
 
• The CPU is the primary component of a computer responsible for executing instructions.
 
• It consists of three main parts: the ALU, CU, and registers.
 
• Registers provide temporary storage for quick data access during processing.
 
 
 
• **Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU):**
 
 
• It is a fundamental part of the CPU that performs all arithmetic and logical operations.
 
• Examples of arithmetic operations include addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division.
 
• Logical operations include comparisons, such as greater than, less than, and equality.
 
 
 
• **Control Unit (CU):**
 
 
• It acts as the "brain" of the CPU, ensuring instruction execution in the correct sequence.
 
• The CU decodes instructions from programs and sends control signals to other components.
 
• It manages communication between the CPU and input/output devices.
 
 
 
• **CPU Architecture:**
 
 
• Modern CPUs use a combination of ALU, CU, and cache memory for efficient data processing.
 
• Multi-core CPUs contain multiple ALUs and CUs to enhance parallel processing and overall performance.
 
• Instruction pipelining is a technique used to improve the execution speed of a CPU.
